subject: research/sensing-epigate
professional: a senior computer-vision / photogrammetry researcher who builds structure-from-motion pipelines (two-view geometric verification, RANSAC variants, bundle adjustment with robust losses); note the field is multi-view geometry, not epidemiology ('epi' = epipolar). First checks: is the normalised 8-point fit and Sampson distance right (Hartley and Zisserman ch. 11), how many matches each verified pair actually has, whether the essential matrix should be used since intrinsics are known, whether the baselines include the obvious ones (pose-informed gate, gate plus RANSAC start), whether spread across seeds is reported, and whether COLMAP/Bundler-style verification is cited as prior art

evidence.correctness: Every number reproduces and the geometry is right. (a) Full rerun: copied the subject and its three sibling dependencies to scratch and ran `python3 experiments/run.py` (10 min 18 s on 4 cores): results.txt byte-identical to the committed file (`diff` empty). (b) Own script scratchpad/epigate/indep.py (does not use the author's F or Sampson for the reference): the true fundamental matrix built from the camera matrices by Hartley-Zisserman eq. 9.1, F = [e']x P' P+, matches the code's RANSAC/normalised 8-point fit on exact matches to 0.00 deg (vectorised angle) for pairs 0-1, 0-2, 0-3; my own loop implementation of H&Z eq. 11.9 Sampson agrees with gate.sampson to 2.4e-12 relative. (c) Noise-only false rejects under the true F at 0.5 px and a 2 px Sampson gate: 6.85e-5 observed vs P(chi2_1 > 16) = 6.33e-5 from the chi-square law. (d) Recomputed recall/lost of the shipped gate with my own counting on the same seeds: 0.9431/0.0223, 0.9256/0.0511, 0.8915/0.1561 at 5/10/20% uniform, identical to results.txt U rows. An independent binomial vote model (a good observation is rejected in a pair iff its partner is mismatched; kept iff accepts >= half its pairs) predicts lost 0.0222/0.0493/0.1172 vs code 0.0223/0.0511/0.1561, and an oracle gate using the true F gives recall 0.993/0.988/0.981 and lost 0.021/0.048/0.120: the code's figures are explained, and the remaining gap is RANSAC fits on tiny pairs (see domain).
evidence.completeness: All README items exist and run: gate.py (mismatch kinds uniform/near/along, normalised 8-point, Sampson, RANSAC, voting gate, run_trial), run.py sections U/N/A/D/E reproducing results.txt exactly, figure.py and error_vs_mismatch.svg, 5 tests (pass in 18 s, README says about 1 min). Live page https://marisstella.app/research/sensing-epigate/ returns 200 and repeats the README headline. Items not done are listed as limitations/next steps (gate + RANSAC start combination, real matcher, focal length), not claimed; later projects sensing-gatemix and sensing-gatecorr took up the real-mismatch step.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q tests`: 5 passed in 17.8 s. Seeded 7 mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: vote comparison >= -> > caught; offsets (1,2,3) -> (1,) caught; dropping the rank-2 projection in _eight SURVIVED; dropping the F^T x2 terms from the Sampson denominator SURVIVED; skipping the inlier refit SURVIVED; counting all removed observations as 'lost' SURVIVED; making 'along' mismatches perpendicular to the epipolar line SURVIVED (the test named test_along_mismatch_lies_on_epipolar_line_of_one_view_only never checks the epipolar line). 5 of 7 survive. No results.txt number is pinned and the shift-range assertion in test_mismatch_kinds runs only for the last kind after the loop.
evidence.craft: Read src/sensing_epigate/gate.py (156 lines), __init__.py, experiments/run.py (60), figure.py, tests/test_gate.py (50), and the sibling sensing_baoutlier/outlier.py it imports. Compact, readable, deterministic, correct vectorised Sampson and Hartley normalisation; reuses the sibling rig instead of copying it. Defects: gate.py:13 inserts sibling src dirs on sys.path while pyproject.toml declares only numpy and scipy, so an installed package cannot import outside the repo tree; mismatch() treats any unknown kind as 'along' and needs cams/pts without checking; run.py reports means only (nanmean) with no spread; test_gate.py:28-29 assertion sits outside the loop.
evidence.claims: Checked 11 claims against results.txt and my rerun. Backed: recall 94/93/89% and lost 2/5/16%; 5% Cauchy 0.168 -> gate+Cauchy 0.0061 (floor 0.0015); RANSAC start 0.012/0.045/0.133; gate at 20% 0.41/0.77; near-miss Cauchy 0.0053 -> 0.0036 and 0.0093 -> 0.0080, recall 84/79%; views 8/12/24 recall 0.73/0.79/0.87, cover 0.87/0.94/1.00, 0.0021 at 24 views; threshold sweep; along 10% Cauchy 0.091 'one bad seed in six' (confirmed: per-seed 0.518 vs five at 0.004-0.007). Not or partly backed: (1) project.json:5 and the live page say near and along mismatches are removed at 79-87%; along at 20% is 0.774. (2) README:3 'plain adjustment after the gate reaches 0.045 against 0.32 without it': 0.32 is Cauchy adjustment without the gate; plain adjustment without the gate is not measured. (3) README:32 'voting over pairs defeats an attack that is consistent with one pair': 40% of visible observations lie in exactly one fitted pair and 38% in two (my count), so for most observations there is no majority vote; along recall 0.79 is below near 0.84 and uniform 0.93. Limitations are honest and prominent (synthetic, own mismatch models, 6 seeds, untuned).
evidence.fitness: A researcher could reuse the gate and the mismatch generators, and two later projects in this repository did (sensing-gatemix, sensing-gatecorr). But the result is not new: two-view geometric verification by RANSAC on F/E/H before bundle adjustment is a fixed stage of every SfM pipeline (Snavely, Seitz, Szeliski 2006 Bundler; Schoenberger and Frahm 2016 COLMAP, which also requires a minimum inlier count per pair), with Lowe's ratio test (2004), LO-RANSAC (Chum et al. 2003), MAGSAC (Barath et al. 2019) and Triggs et al. (2000) on robust BA; none of these is cited (only H&Z and Fischler-Bolles). The one non-obvious comparison, gate vs a per-point RANSAC triangulation start, is run on a rig whose pairs have a median of 22 shared points, so it does not transfer to real pipelines with hundreds of matches per pair. One session, not part of a programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md; well below the research/CLAUDE.md PhD bar.
evidence.domain: Method details a reviewer checks first are right: Hartley normalisation, rank-2 projection, denormalisation T2^T F T1, Sampson distance and a chi-square-consistent 2 px threshold. Departures: (1) intrinsics are known, so the standard tool is the essential matrix (Nister 2004 five-point), not the 7-dof F; (2) on the 12-view rig 26% of the gate's view pairs have fewer than 8 shared points and are skipped and 37% have under 15 (scratchpad/epigate/overlap.py), so many F fits have 0-6 redundant points; COLMAP's default needs 15 inliers. That, not the threshold, is why recall is 0.93 instead of the 0.99 an oracle F gives and why good-observation loss at 20% is 16% vs 12%; the README never reports matches per pair; (3) the approximate poses are ignored by design, but a pose-informed epipolar gate with a loose threshold is the obvious baseline and is absent, as is gate + RANSAC start; (4) only means over 6 seeds, no spread: at 10% uniform the gate+Cauchy mean 0.079 is one seed at 0.387 (median 0.022 vs RANSAC-start median 0.041), so the 'not better than the RANSAC start' ordering at 10% rests on one seed (the README does say it is unresolved).

verdict: A small, correct synthetic study: results.txt reproduces byte-identically (10 min on 4 cores), the fitted F matches the true F from the cameras by H&Z eq. 9.1, the Sampson distance matches eq. 11.9, the noise false-reject rate matches the chi-square law, and the recall and good-observation loss recompute exactly and are explained by an independent vote model and an oracle-F gate. The headline numbers can be trusted for this rig. Three things keep it from the bar. The tests miss most seeded bugs (5 of 7 survive). The rig verifies view pairs with a median of 22 shared points, a quarter of pairs under 8, which drives the recall and loss figures and keeps the gate-vs-RANSAC-start comparison from transferring to real pipelines. And the work is a standard SfM stage, with no SfM prior art cited, no seed spread reported, and F used even though intrinsics are known. Correctness 3, claims 3, verification 1: it does not meet the bar. It is finished as a one-session synthetic note, well below the research PhD bar.
